report_md:
# Multi-horizon quiet capitulation reversal — report

**Slug:** `capitulation-reversal-v2`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29 (development only; the 2024-2026 holdout
was not loaded by this agent). Note: a `holdout.json` and `holdout_run.log`
appeared in this folder at 04:30 from a separate process after the development
run; this agent did not read or use them.
**Execution:** `research/bt.py`, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band,
long-only, weights >= 0, sum <= 1. Headline cost 1 bp; 5 bp and 10 bp also
reported.
**Primary:** QQQ -3% over 3 sessions **or** -5% over 10 **or** -8% over 15, on
volume <= 1.2x the prior 20-day average; buy TQQQ at the event-day close; hold
one session.

---

## 1. Headline

| cost | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | vol | TQQQ exposure | fills | turnover |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **1 bp** | **39.75%** | **26.44%** | **1.46** | **2.26** | 25.1% | **5.88%** | 743 | 4257x |
| 5 bp | 34.67% | 28.18% | 1.32 | 2.02 | 25.1% | 5.88% | 743 | 3508x |
| 10 bp | 28.58% | 30.30% | 1.13 | 1.72 | 25.0% | 5.88% | 743 | 2777x |

The stated bar is TQQQ 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% max DD / 0.82 Sharpe. **At 1 bp the
primary passes both legs** (39.75% > 36.72%, 26.44% < 82.29%). **At 5 bp it
fails the CAGR leg** (34.67% < 36.72%) while still beating the drawdown leg by
54 pp. The local `bt.benchmark` TQQQ is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80; the 0.57 pp
difference from the task's 36.72% is a bar-convention difference, and the
strategy clears both figures at 1 bp.

The strategy holds TQQQ on 5.88% of bars (119 events, one session each) and
BIL otherwise. Ending equity at 1 bp is $1,447,614 from $100,000.

## 2. Benchmarks

| | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe | Calmar |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| strategy 1 bp | 39.75% | 26.44% | 1.46 | 1.50 |
| TQQQ | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 0.44 |
| QQQ | 18.91% | 37.30% | 0.90 | 0.51 |
| 165-day QQQ SMA baseline | 44.76% | 58.76% | 1.03 | 0.76 |

Daily-return correlation is **0.392 to TQQQ** and **0.061 to the 165-day
baseline**. The strategy is a diversifying, cash-heavy sleeve; it does not beat
the 165-day baseline on CAGR (39.75% vs 44.76%) but has a much lower drawdown
(26.4% vs 58.8%) and a higher Sharpe (1.46 vs 1.03).

## 3. Yearly returns

| year | strategy | TQQQ | note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2016 | +12.5% | +19.9% | 4 events |
| 2017 | +0.7% | +114.5% | no real event; cash drag |
| 2018 | +40.1% | -20.8% | 14 events, 78% win |
| 2019 | +17.0% | +148.2% | 4 events |
| 2020 | +178.4% | +104.1% | 20 events, +5.7% mean |
| 2021 | -3.6% | +81.1% | 2 events, mean -1.0%; one large loss |
| 2022 | +117.5% | -79.4% | 67 events, +1.6% mean |
| 2023 | +33.6% | +192.0% | 8 events, 88% win |

Six of eight years are positive. The strategy's best years are the volatile,
mean-reverting ones (2018, 2020, 2022); it lags badly in calm bull years (2017,
2019, 2023), which is expected for a 5.9%-exposure sleeve. The 2021 loss is two
events with a mean of -1.0% (one large loss, one small gain), so it is not
evidence of a broken edge, but it is also not a meaningful sample.

## 4. Event study

119 events. Entry at the event-day 15:59 open, exit at the next session's 15:59
open:

| statistic | value |
|---|---:|
| mean | +2.60% |
| median | +2.07% |
| win rate | 64.7% |
| t-stat | 4.33 |
| bootstrap 95% CI | +1.42% .. +3.76% |
| bootstrap p(mean <= 0) | 0.0000 |
| worst / best | -14.40% / +22.20% |

**Decomposition:**

| leg | mean | t | win |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| overnight 15:59 -> 09:30 | +0.80% | 2.30 | 58% |
| intraday 09:30 -> 15:59 | +1.78% | 3.77 | 66% |
| full close-to-close | +2.60% | 4.33 | 65% |

Both legs are positive; the intraday leg is larger. The close entry captures the
0.80% overnight that a next-open entry would miss. This is the main reason the
close-entry design beats the earlier next-open version.

**By leg combination (rows overlap; the single-leg rows are exclusive of the
deeper legs):**

| leg | n | mean | win |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| q3 only | 34 | +1.48% | 59% |
| q10 only | 31 | +2.11% | 68% |
| q15 only | 11 | +4.39% | 91% |
| q10 & q15 | 25 | +5.38% | 72% |
| all three | 8 | +6.99% | 75% |

The deeper and overlapping events carry the strongest returns. The q3-only
sleeve is the weakest part of the primary; it adds event count and
diversification, not the core edge.

**By year:**

| year | n | mean | win |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | 4 | +3.21% | 75% |
| 2018 | 14 | +2.73% | 79% |
| 2019 | 4 | +3.84% | 75% |
| 2020 | 20 | +5.70% | 75% |
| 2021 | 2 | -1.00% | 50% |
| 2022 | 67 | +1.59% | 55% |
| 2023 | 8 | +3.03% | 88% |

The per-event mean is positive in every year with n >= 4. 2022 has the most
events and the weakest per-event mean; its large P&L contribution comes from
frequency (67 events), not from a higher edge.

## 5. Pre-registered grid and plateau

All at 1 bp, 1-minute marks.

| # | variant | n | exposure | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | core q10 only | 71 | 3.50% | 28.85% | 17.01% | 1.33 |
| 2 | core q15 only | 39 | 1.93% | 22.99% | 15.42% | 1.29 |
| 3 | core q10 \| q15 | 85 | 4.19% | 34.53% | 16.87% | 1.46 |
| 4 | **primary** (q3 \| q10 \| q15) | 119 | 5.88% | **39.75%** | **26.44%** | **1.46** |
| 5 | primary, q3 -2.5% | 129 | 6.33% | 41.09% | 26.44% | 1.48 |
| 6 | primary, q3 -3.5% | 109 | 5.38% | 38.74% | 21.09% | 1.47 |
| 7 | primary, rvol 1.15 | 102 | 5.03% | 30.63% | 26.44% | 1.31 |
| 8 | primary, rvol 1.25 | 131 | 6.42% | 27.50% | 38.38% | 1.01 |

The **q3 threshold is a plateau**: rows 4-6 give 38.7-41.1% CAGR, 21-26% DD and
Sharpe 1.47-1.48. The **volume cap is a cliff**: 1.15 gives 30.6%, 1.20 gives
39.75%, 1.25 gives 27.5% with a 38.4% DD. The 1.2 cutoff is the fragile
parameter. The core without q3 is 34.53% / 16.87% / 1.46 at 1 bp; its cost
sensitivity is 31.05% / 17.80% / 1.35 at 5 bp and 26.82% / 19.09% / 1.20 at
10 bp.

## 6. Placebo

200 random-event backtests with the same count (119), entry (event close), hold
(one session) and size rule:

| | value |
|---|---:|
| placebo mean CAGR | 1.73% |
| placebo sd | 5.47% |
| placebo p95 | 10.71% |
| placebo max | 16.08% |
| p(real >= placebo) | 0.000 |

The real 39.75% is far outside the random-event distribution. The event timing,
not the 5.9% exposure or the close-entry mechanics, carries the result.

## 7. Cut tests and concentration

| period | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016-2019 | 16.77% | 12.54% | 1.38 |
| 2020-2021 | 64.11% | 15.39% | 1.77 |
| 2022-2023 | 71.19% | 26.44% | 1.67 |
| ex-2020 | 22.99% | 26.44% | 1.14 |
| ex-2022 | 27.02% | 15.39% | 1.44 |

The strategy is positive in all three sub-periods, but 2022-2023 dominates.
Excluding 2020 or 2022 still leaves 23-27% CAGR with a 15-26% DD, so the edge is
not a single year; the point estimate is still regime-tilted.

**Top-event concentration:**

| exclusion | CAGR | max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| none | 39.75% | 26.44% | 1.46 |
| top 1 event | 36.45% | 26.44% | 1.38 |
| top 3 events | 30.09% | 26.44% | 1.25 |
| top 5 events | 25.74% | 26.44% | 1.11 |
| top 10 events | 17.14% | 26.74% | 0.83 |

Removing the single best event puts the CAGR at 36.45%, i.e. essentially at the
bar; removing the top three drops it to 30.1%. The 1 bp pass depends on a
handful of large events. This is the second fragility, alongside the volume
cliff.

The maximum drawdown is -26.44%, from 2022-03-08 to 2022-05-04 — a 2022
event-cluster drawdown, not a 2020 crash. It is well inside the 82.29% TQQQ
drawdown but is the reason the strategy is not a low-vol replacement for cash.

## 8. Causality and implementation

- All signals use QQQ data through **15:58 ET**; the target is written on the
  15:58 bar and fills at the **15:59 open**. The signal is not computed from
  the official 16:00 close.
- Daily volume is summed through 15:58, not the full session, so the volume
  ratio is causal.
- Truncating the panel at **2022-01-03** leaves every prior weight identical
  (586,637 bars compared). No full-sample normalization, no future data.
- The 2024-2026 holdout was never loaded; the panel's end is 2023-12-29.

## 9. Sample adequacy

119 events over 8 years, ~15/year, 5.9% of sessions, one session each. The
event mean is +2.60% with t = 4.33 and a bootstrap CI of +1.42% to +3.76%; that
is large enough to reject a zero mean. It is **not** large enough to rule out
regime dependence: 87 of 119 events (73%) are in 2020-2022, and 2021 has two
events. The q3-only leg has 34 events and a +1.48% mean; the q10/q15 core has 85
events and a +3.05% mean (t=4.23). The core is the statistically stronger
object; the q3 leg is the diversifying sleeve.

## 10. Honest verdict

**Marginal 1 bp pass. Not a validated standalone.**

- It clears the stated bar at 1 bp: 39.75% vs 36.72% CAGR, 26.44% vs 82.29% max
  DD, Sharpe 1.46 vs 0.82, Calmar 1.50 vs 0.44.
- It fails the CAGR leg at 5 bp (34.67%) and 10 bp (28.58%).
- The volume cap at 1.2 is a cliff; the P&L is concentrated in the top 3-5
  events; 73% of events are in 2020-2022. The pass is not robust enough to
  promote without the holdout.
- The **robust core** (q10/q15, no q3) is 34.53% / 16.87% / 1.46 at 1 bp, 31.05%
  at 5 bp, 26.82% at 10 bp. It is a clean risk-adjusted improvement — Sharpe
  1.46 vs 0.80, Calmar 2.05 vs 0.44, DD 16.9% vs 82.3% — at the cost of 5.2 pp
  of CAGR versus the primary, and 2.2 pp below the bar. If robustness matters
  more than the headline, the core is the better strategy.
- The honest description is: a **marginal 1 bp TQQQ-beater with a strong
  risk-adjusted profile and two known fragilities**, not a clean replacement
  for TQQQ. Do not quote the 39.75% as a validated result until the holdout is
  run on the frozen file.

## 11. What it is not

It is not `gap-capitulation-reversal` with a new parameter: the event horizon
(3/10/15-day cumulative vs one-day close/intraday), entry (close vs next open),
hold (1 vs 3 sessions), vehicle (always TQQQ vs QQQ/TQQQ switch) and exit (time
only vs event-low + hard stop) are all different. It is not
`intraday-mean-reversion` (no intraday trigger; close-to-close hold), and not
`gap-fill-fade` (long TQQQ; no gap fade; no short). It uses no 165-day base, no
old stop and no old weight matrix; the 165-day baseline appears only in the
correlation/benchmark table.

## 12. Files

- `HYPOTHESIS.md` — mechanism, exact rules, falsifiers, pre-registered grid.
- `strategy.py` — `build_weights(ts, o, c)` and `main()`; writes `result.json`.
- `result.json` — metrics, event dates, grid, cuts, placebo, yearly.
- `report.md` — this file.
hypothesis_md:
# Multi-horizon quiet capitulation reversal — `capitulation-reversal-v2`

**Status:** pre-registered. Development window only, 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29.
The 2024-2026 holdout has not been loaded or inspected.
**Primary:** `q3 <= -3.0%` or `q10 <= -5.0%` or `q15 <= -8.0%`, volume <= 1.2x the
prior 20-day average, buy TQQQ at the event-day close, hold one session.

---

## 1. What is genuinely new

The existing `gap-capitulation-reversal` (v1) is a **one-day** event: QQQ closes
<= -2% or trades <= -3% intraday, with a 20-day oversold condition and a
quiet-volume filter; it holds TQQQ (or QQQ when vol > 30%) for **three**
sessions, and it enters at the **next open**. It produced 30 events, ~4%
exposure and 8.3% CAGR at 1 bp on the development window.

This v2 keeps the broad area — a quiet decline is a positioning event that
reverses — and changes every part of the implementation:

| | v1 `gap-capitulation-reversal` | v2 `capitulation-reversal-v2` |
|---|---|---|
| Event horizon | one session (close or intraday low) | **cumulative 3, 10 or 15 sessions** |
| Event thresholds | -2% close / -3% low / 20-day -3% | **-3% / -5% / -8% cumulative** |
| Volume | <= 1.2x 20-day | <= 1.2x 20-day (same prior, new horizon) |
| Entry | next session's open | **event-day close (15:59)** |
| Hold | 3 sessions | **1 session** |
| Vehicle | TQQQ only when QQQ vol <= 30%, else QQQ | **always TQQQ, vol-capped** |
| Size | 100% of the chosen asset | 100% TQQQ capped by `0.80 / vol20` |
| Exit | time + event-low + 8% stop | time only (one session) |
| Events / exposure | 30 / 3.9% | **119 / 5.9%** |

It is also distinct from the other named rebuilds:

- `intraday-mean-reversion`: that is a **one-day intraday** QQQ -3% trigger,
  next-open entry, same-session exit, and never holds overnight. v2 has no
  intraday trigger, uses multi-day cumulative declines, and holds
  close-to-close (including the overnight).
- `gap-fill-fade`: that is a **short QQQ** trade on failed small gap-ups inside
  a weak tape. v2 is long TQQQ, uses no gap, no opening range and no short.
- The old 165-day QQQ base and the old 4% stop are **not used**. The 165-day
  baseline is computed only for the correlation/benchmark table.

## 2. Mechanism

1. **A multi-day decline on below-average volume is an air pocket, not news.**
   If the decline were information-driven, volume would be high and the next
   session would continue to reprice. Quiet volume means the decline is a
   drift/positioning event: sellers are not urgent, buyers are absent, and the
   next session's opening flow reverses the drift. This is the same family as
   the v1 quiet-volume prior, but applied to a multi-session cumulative decline
   rather than a single close or intraday low.
2. **The reversal is realised in the next close-to-close return, including the
   overnight.** A next-open entry misses the overnight gap. On the v1 event,
   the close-entry version earns roughly 30% CAGR at 1 bp versus 18% for the
   next-open version; the overnight is a large part of the reversal. The v2
   implementation therefore computes the signal at 15:58 and fills at the 15:59
   open, and exits at the next session's 15:59 open.
3. **TQQQ gives 3x the reversal; the one-session hold avoids the fade.** The
   event study shows the first session carries the edge and sessions 2-5 give
   it back. A one-session hold is not a compromise; it is the measured optimum.
4. **Three horizons capture fast, medium and slow quiet declines.** The 3-day
   leg catches shallow pullbacks (often in bull markets), the 10-day leg the
   normal multi-day pullback, and the 15-day -8% leg the deeper capitulation.
   The three legs are highly overlapping but not identical; the union raises
   the event count from 85 to 119 without destroying the per-event mean.

## 3. Hypothesis (one sentence)

On 2016-01-04 .. 2023-12-29, a QQQ decline of at least 3% over 3 sessions, 5%
over 10 sessions, or 8% over 15 sessions, on volume at most 1.2x the prior
20-day average, is followed by a positive next-session TQQQ close-to-close
return large enough that a 100% TQQQ position held only on those event days
beats TQQQ's 36.72% development CAGR with a much lower maximum drawdown.

## 4. Exact rules

Data: QQQ (signal), TQQQ (vehicle), BIL (cash); adjusted 1-minute regular
session. All signals use only data through 15:58 ET; all fills are at the next
bar's open by `research/bt.py`.

At 15:58 ET on session `d`:

```
q3   = QQQ_close_1558[d] / QQQ_close_1558[d-3]  - 1
q10  = QQQ_close_1558[d] / QQQ_close_1558[d-10] - 1
q15  = QQQ_close_1558[d] / QQQ_close_1558[d-15] - 1
rvol = volume_1558[d] / mean(volume_1558[d-20 .. d-1])
vol20 = annualised stdev(QQQ daily returns, last 20 sessions)
```

Event:

```
(q3 <= -3.0% OR q10 <= -5.0% OR q15 <= -8.0%) AND rvol <= 1.2
```

If the event is true:

- **Entry:** set the TQQQ target on the 15:58 bar, so it fills at the 15:59
  open. Size = `clip(0.80 / vol20, 0.25, 1.0)`.
- **Hold:** through the next session.
- **Exit:** set the target to 0 on the next session's 15:58 bar, so it fills at
  the 15:59 open.
- **Chain:** if the exit day is itself an event, the new event's entry
  overwrites the exit and the position stays on for another session.
- Otherwise 100% BIL. Long-only, weights >= 0, sum <= 1. No leverage beyond
  TQQQ's embedded 3x.

## 5. Why it should beat TQQQ

TQQQ's 36.72% CAGR comes with an 82.29% drawdown. v2 is in TQQQ only ~6% of
sessions and in BIL otherwise, so its drawdown should be far lower. The
measured event mean is +2.6% per event with a t-stat near 4; 119 events at 5.9%
exposure can compound to roughly 40% CAGR at 1 bp. The risk-adjusted case is
stronger than the absolute-CAGR case: the target is a Sharpe around 1.4 and a
Calmar around 1.5-2.0, versus 0.82 and 0.45 for TQQQ.

## 6. What would falsify it

1. **No event edge.** Mean next-session TQQQ return <= 0, or bootstrap
   `p(mean <= 0) > 0.05`.
2. **Placebo matches.** Random sessions with the same count, entry, hold and
   size produce a CAGR within the 90% band of the real strategy.
3. **One episode.** Excluding 2020 or 2022 drops CAGR below 10%, or the
   per-year event mean is negative in more than one year with n >= 3.
4. **Knife-edge grid.** The q3 -2.5%/-3.5% and q15 -7%/-8% neighbours all
   collapse below 20% CAGR.
5. **Costs dominate.** 10 bp CAGR < 15%, or 10 bp max drawdown > 40%.
6. **Look-ahead.** Truncating the panel at 2022-01-03 changes any prior weight.
7. **The volume cap is a cliff.** rvol 1.15 and 1.25 both collapse relative to
   1.20. This is the known fragility of the design; it must be reported, not
   hidden.

## 7. Pre-registered grid (8 combinations)

All at 1 bp, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band. The primary is row 4.
Rows 1-3 are the core without the short-horizon leg; rows 5-6 vary the q3
threshold; rows 7-8 vary the volume cap.

| # | q3 | q10 | q15 | rvol | hold | expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | off | -5% | off | 1.2 | 1 | core, ~29% CAGR / ~17% DD |
| 2 | off | off | -8% | 1.2 | 1 | core, ~23% CAGR / ~15% DD |
| 3 | off | -5% | -8% | 1.2 | 1 | core, ~34% CAGR / ~17% DD |
| 4 | -3% | -5% | -8% | 1.2 | 1 | **primary, ~40% CAGR / ~26% DD** |
| 5 | -2.5% | -5% | -8% | 1.2 | 1 | more events, ~41% CAGR / ~26% DD |
| 6 | -3.5% | -5% | -8% | 1.2 | 1 | fewer events, ~39% CAGR / ~21% DD |
| 7 | -3% | -5% | -8% | 1.15 | 1 | tighter volume, ~31% CAGR / ~26% DD |
| 8 | -3% | -5% | -8% | 1.25 | 1 | looser volume, ~28% CAGR / ~38% DD |

The expected plateau is rows 3-6: 34-41% CAGR with 17-26% DD. Rows 7-8 are
expected to be worse; the 1.2 volume cap is the fragile parameter, not the q3
threshold (rows 4-6 should be a plateau).

**Disclosure:** the expectations above are priors from a development-only event
study that motivated the design, not an independent sample. The final run uses
the same 2016-2023 window, so the agreement between the prior and the observed
values is not out-of-sample validation. The grid is pre-registered in the sense
that the primary and all eight rows were fixed before the final 1-minute run,
and no row was dropped or added after it.

## 8. Honest prior

The most likely outcome is a **marginal 1 bp pass**: the primary is expected to
land around 39-40% CAGR with a 26% drawdown, while the 5 bp result will be
around 34-35%, just below the TQQQ bar. The robust core (rows 1-3) is expected
to be 29-35% CAGR with a 15-17% drawdown — a clear risk-adjusted improvement,
not an absolute pass. The q3 leg is statistically weaker than the q10/q15 core
(mean +1.48%, t≈1.4 versus +3.05%, t=4.23), so part of the primary's pass is a
diversifying short-horizon sleeve, not a stronger capitulation edge. 2020 and
2022 supply most of the events (20 and 67 of 119); the per-year event mean is
positive in every year with n >= 4, but the sample is regime-tilted. Treat the
result as a candidate that needs the holdout, not as a validated standalone.

## 9. Sample adequacy

119 events over 8 years, ~15/year, 5.9% of sessions, 1 session each. The event
mean is +2.62% with t = 4.35 and a bootstrap 95% CI of +1.45% to +3.79%. That
is large enough to reject a zero mean, but not large enough to rule out regime
dependence: 73% of the events are in 2020-2022, and the 2021 sample is two
events. The report states this explicitly.

Idea
----
A multi-session QQQ decline on *below-average* volume is a positioning / air
pocket, not an information event.  The reversal is realised in the next
session's close-to-close return, including the overnight gap, so the trade is
entered at the event-day close (15:59) and held for one session.

Event at 15:58 ET on session d:
    q3   = QQQ_close_1558[d] / QQQ_close_1558[d-3]  - 1
    q10  = QQQ_close_1558[d] / QQQ_close_1558[d-10] - 1
    q15  = QQQ_close_1558[d] / QQQ_close_1558[d-15] - 1
    rvol = volume_1558[d] / mean(volume_1558[d-20 .. d-1])
    event = (q3 <= -3.0% OR q10 <= -5.0% OR q15 <= -8.0%) AND rvol <= 1.2

Entry: TQQQ at the 15:59 open of the event day, size = clip(0.80/vol20, 0.25, 1).
Exit:  at the 15:59 open of the next session.  If that session is also an
event, the new entry chains and the position stays on for another session.

No 100-250 day moving average is used by the strategy.  The 165-day baseline is
computed only for the correlation/benchmark table.  No old weight matrix or
old `build_weights` is imported.

Run:
    $env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\\Users\\27175\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\opencode\\pylibs"
    python research/new/capitulation-reversal-v2/strategy.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

DEV_START, DEV_END = "2016-01-04", "2023-12-29"
BARS_PER_YEAR = 252 * 390
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

# Pre-registered primary.  The grid in HYPOTHESIS.md varies q3 / rvol_max.
PARAMS = dict(
    q3=-0.030,
    q10=-0.050,
    q15=-0.080,
    rvol_max=1.20,
    hold=1,
    vol_target=0.80,
    size_floor=0.25,
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# daily features (all known at 15:58)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def daily_volume_1558(ts: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> np.ndarray:
    """QQQ volume through 15:58, one value per session of `ts`."""
    q = bt.load_1m("QQQ")
    lo = pd.Timestamp(ts[0].date(), tz="America/New_York")
    hi = pd.Timestamp(ts[-1].date(), tz="America/New_York") + pd.Timedelta(days=1)
    q = q[(q["ts"] >= lo) & (q["ts"] < hi)].copy()
    q = q[q["ts"].dt.time < pd.Timestamp("15:59").time()]
    q["date"] = q["date"].astype("datetime64[ns]")
    sess = pd.DatetimeIndex(sorted(set(pd.Timestamp(t.date()) for t in ts)))
    return q.groupby("date")["volume"].sum().reindex(sess).to_numpy()


def daily_features(ts, o, c):
    """Return the daily signal frame aligned to `ts`'s sessions."""
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    nd = len(first)
    qc = c[last - 1, 0]                       # QQQ 15:58 close
    qret = np.r_[np.nan, qc[1:] / qc[:-1] - 1.0]
    q3 = pd.Series(qc).pct_change(3).to_numpy()
    q10 = pd.Series(qc).pct_change(10).to_numpy()
    q15 = pd.Series(qc).pct_change(15).to_numpy()
    vol20 = pd.Series(qret).rolling(20).std(ddof=0).to_numpy() * np.sqrt(252.0)
    qvol = daily_volume_1558(ts)
    rvol = qvol / pd.Series(qvol).shift(1).rolling(20).mean().to_numpy()
    return dict(dates=dates, first=first, last=last, nd=nd,
                q3=q3, q10=q10, q15=q15, vol20=vol20, rvol=rvol, qvol=qvol)


def event_mask(f: dict, p: dict) -> np.ndarray:
    """Pre-registered event mask.  None disables a leg (grid only)."""
    nd = f["nd"]
    ev = np.zeros(nd, dtype=bool)
    if p.get("q3") is not None:
        ev |= f["q3"] <= p["q3"]
    if p.get("q10") is not None:
        ev |= f["q10"] <= p["q10"]
    if p.get("q15") is not None:
        ev |= f["q15"] <= p["q15"]
    finite = (np.isfinite(f["rvol"]) & np.isfinite(f["vol20"]))
    return ev & (f["rvol"] <= p["rvol_max"]) & finite


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# weights
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _size(f: dict, d: int, p: dict) -> float:
    return float(np.clip(p["vol_target"] / max(f["vol20"][d], 0.01),
                         p["size_floor"], 1.0))


def _weights_from_mask(ts, o, c, f: dict, mask: np.ndarray, p: dict):
    """Build the (n, 3) weight matrix for an arbitrary event mask."""
    n = len(ts)
    nd, first, last = f["nd"], f["first"], f["last"]
    hold = int(p["hold"])
    w = np.zeros((n, 3))
    w[:, 2] = 1.0                              # BIL by default
    for d in range(25, nd - hold):
        if not mask[d]:
            continue
        sz = _size(f, d, p)
        le = int(last[d])
        # Entry: target on the 15:58 bar -> fill at the 15:59 open.
        w[le - 1, 1] = sz
        w[le - 1, 2] = 1.0 - sz
        # Hold through the next `hold` sessions.
        for s in range(d + 1, d + hold + 1):
            fs, ls = int(first[s]), int(last[s])
            w[fs:ls, 1] = sz
            w[fs:ls, 2] = 1.0 - sz
        # Exit: target 0 on the 15:58 bar of the last held session.
        le2 = int(last[d + hold])
        w[le2 - 1, 1] = 0.0
        w[le2 - 1, 2] = 1.0
    return w


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params=None):
    """Return (weights (n,3), info).  See HYPOTHESIS.md for the exact rules."""
    p = dict(PARAMS)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    f = daily_features(ts, o, c)
    mask = event_mask(f, p)
    w = _weights_from_mask(ts, o, c, f, mask, p)
    event_dates = [str(f["dates"][f["last"][d]]) for d in range(25, f["nd"] - p["hold"])
                   if mask[d]]
    sizes = [_size(f, d, p) for d in range(25, f["nd"] - p["hold"]) if mask[d]]
    info = dict(
        params=p,
        n_events=int(mask.sum()),
        event_dates=event_dates,
        exposure=float(np.mean(w[:, 1])),
        mean_size=float(np.mean(sizes)) if sizes else None,
        min_size=float(np.min(sizes)) if sizes else None,
    )
    return w, info


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# benchmark only (not part of the strategy)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def benchmark_weights(ts, c, n=165):
    """165-day QQQ SMA baseline, used ONLY for the correlation/benchmark."""
    dates = bt.session_dates(ts)
    first = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, dates[1:] != dates[:-1]])
    last = np.r_[first[1:] - 1, len(ts) - 1]
    qc = c[last, 0]
    sma = pd.Series(qc).rolling(n).mean().to_numpy()
    reg = np.zeros(len(first), bool)
    reg[1:] = qc[:-1] > sma[:-1]
    day_id = np.repeat(np.arange(len(first)), np.diff(np.r_[first, len(ts)]))
    w = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    w[:, 1] = reg[day_id].astype(float)
    w[:, 2] = 1.0 - w[:, 1]
    return w


def daily_returns(result):
    eq = pd.Series(result["equity"], index=result["ts"])
    return eq.groupby(eq.index.date).last().pct_change().dropna()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# evaluation helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _metrics(w, slip=1.0, start=DEV_START, end=DEV_END):
    if start == DEV_START and end == DEV_END:
        # The development panel already ends at DEV_END; using bt.run keeps
        # the last session, so yearly() sees the same index as the equity.
        r = bt.run(ts_global, o_global, c_global, w, start,
                   band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
        s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
        s["tqqq_exposure"] = float(np.mean(w[:, 1]))
        return r, s
    i = bt.start_index(ts_global, start)
    j = int(ts_global.searchsorted(pd.Timestamp(end, tz="America/New_York"), side="right"))
    r = bt.simulate(ts_global[i:j], o_global[i:j], c_global[i:j], w[i:j],
                    band=0.02, slippage_bps=slip)
    s = bt.stats(r, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    s["tqqq_exposure"] = float(np.mean(w[i:j, 1]))
    return r, s


def _event_stats(f, mask, hold=1):
    Rs = []
    for d in range(25, f["nd"] - hold):
        if not mask[d]:
            continue
        entry = o_global[f["last"][d], 1]       # 15:59 open of event day
        exit_ = o_global[f["last"][d + hold], 1]  # 15:59 open of exit day
        Rs.append(float(exit_ / entry - 1.0))
    Rs = np.asarray(Rs)
    if len(Rs) < 3:
        return {"n": int(len(Rs))}
    t = float(Rs.mean() / Rs.std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(len(Rs))) if Rs.std(ddof=1) > 0 else None
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    boot = rng.choice(Rs, (10000, len(Rs)), replace=True).mean(axis=1)
    return {
        "n": int(len(Rs)),
        "mean": float(Rs.mean()),
        "median": float(np.median(Rs)),
        "win": float((Rs > 0).mean()),
        "t": t,
        "bootstrap_p": float((boot <= 0).mean()),
        "ci95_low": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.025)),
        "ci95_high": float(np.quantile(boot, 0.975)),
        "worst": float(Rs.min()),
        "best": float(Rs.max()),
    }


def _placebo(f, n_events, n_draws=200, seed=11):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    all_days = np.arange(25, f["nd"] - 1)
    cagrs = []
    for _ in range(n_draws):
        pick = rng.choice(all_days, n_events, replace=False)
        m = np.zeros(f["nd"], bool)
        m[pick] = True
        w = _weights_from_mask(ts_global, o_global, c_global, f, m, PARAMS)
        _, s = _metrics(w, 1.0)
        cagrs.append(s["cagr"])
    cagrs = np.asarray(cagrs)
    return {
        "n_draws": int(n_draws),
        "mean": float(cagrs.mean()),
        "std": float(cagrs.std(ddof=1)),
        "p95": float(np.quantile(cagrs, 0.95)),
        "max": float(cagrs.max()),
        "p_value": float((cagrs >= _metrics(build_weights(ts_global, o_global, c_global)[0], 1.0)[1]["cagr"]).mean()),
    }


def _cut(w, start, end, slip=1.0):
    return _metrics(w, slip, start, end)[1]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ts_global = o_global = c_global = None


def main():
    global ts_global, o_global, c_global
    ts_global, o_global, c_global = bt.panel(
        ("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"), DEV_START, DEV_END, "1min")
    ts, o, c = ts_global, o_global, c_global

    w, info = build_weights(ts, o, c)
    f = daily_features(ts, o, c)
    mask = event_mask(f, PARAMS)

    out = {
        "agent": "capitulation-reversal-v2",
        "idea": "A multi-session QQQ decline on below-average volume is a "
                "positioning event, not news; it reverses in the next session's "
                "close-to-close return, so buy TQQQ at the event close and hold "
                "one session.",
        "hypothesis": "QQQ -3% over 3 sessions, -5% over 10, or -8% over 15, on "
                      "volume <= 1.2x the prior 20-day average, is followed by a "
                      "positive next-session TQQQ return large enough to beat "
                      "TQQQ's 36.72% development CAGR with a lower drawdown.",
        "universe": ["QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL"],
        "window": {"dev": [DEV_START, DEV_END], "holdout": "not loaded"},
        "params": PARAMS,
        "info": info,
        "windows": {"dev": {}},
        "benchmarks": {},
        "event_study": _event_stats(f, mask),
        "event_study_by_year": {},
        "grid": [],
        "cuts": {},
        "yearly": {},
        "corr_tqqq": None,
        "corr_165d": None,
    }

    r1 = None
    for slip, lab in ((1.0, "1bp"), (5.0, "5bp"), (10.0, "10bp")):
        r, s = _metrics(w, slip)
        out["windows"]["dev"][lab] = {
            "cagr": s["cagr"], "max_drawdown": s["max_drawdown"],
            "sharpe": s["sharpe"], "sortino": s["sortino"],
            "volatility": s["volatility"], "fills": s["fills"],
            "turnover": s["turnover"], "ending_equity": s["ending_equity"],
            "tqqq_exposure": s["tqqq_exposure"],
        }
        if slip == 1.0:
            r1 = r

    # yearly and correlations
    y = bt.yearly(ts, r1["equity"], c[:, 1])
    out["yearly"] = {int(k): {"strategy": v["strategy"], "benchmark": v["benchmark"]}
                     for k, v in y.items()}
    sr = daily_returns(r1)
    tr = pd.Series(c[:, 1], index=ts)
    tr = tr.groupby(tr.index.date).last().pct_change().dropna()
    j = sr.index.intersection(tr.index)
    out["corr_tqqq"] = float(np.corrcoef(sr.loc[j], tr.loc[j])[0, 1])

    bw = benchmark_weights(ts, c)
    rb, sb = _metrics(bw, 1.0)
    br = daily_returns(rb)
    j2 = sr.index.intersection(br.index)
    out["corr_165d"] = float(np.corrcoef(sr.loc[j2], br.loc[j2])[0, 1])

    out["benchmarks"]["tqqq"] = bt.benchmark(c[:, 1], ts, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    out["benchmarks"]["qqq"] = bt.benchmark(c[:, 0], ts, BARS_PER_YEAR)
    out["benchmarks"]["baseline_165d"] = {
        "cagr": sb["cagr"], "max_drawdown": sb["max_drawdown"],
        "sharpe": sb["sharpe"], "volatility": sb["volatility"],
    }

    # event study by year
    years = {}
    for d in range(25, f["nd"] - 1):
        if not mask[d]:
            continue
        yr = int(pd.Timestamp(f["dates"][f["last"][d]]).year)
        yrs = years.setdefault(yr, [])
        yrs.append(float(o_global[f["last"][d + 1], 1] /
                         o_global[f["last"][d], 1] - 1.0))
    out["event_study_by_year"] = {
        int(yr): {"n": len(v), "mean": float(np.mean(v)),
                  "win": float((np.asarray(v) > 0).mean())}
        for yr, v in sorted(years.items())
    }

    # pre-registered grid
    grid = [
        ("1 core q10", dict(q3=None, q10=-0.05, q15=None, rvol_max=1.20, hold=1)),
        ("2 core q15", dict(q3=None, q10=None, q15=-0.08, rvol_max=1.20, hold=1)),
        ("3 core union", dict(q3=None, q10=-0.05, q15=-0.08, rvol_max=1.20, hold=1)),
        ("4 primary", dict(q3=-0.03, q10=-0.05, q15=-0.08, rvol_max=1.20, hold=1)),
        ("5 q3 -2.5%", dict(q3=-0.025, q10=-0.05, q15=-0.08, rvol_max=1.20, hold=1)),
        ("6 q3 -3.5%", dict(q3=-0.035, q10=-0.05, q15=-0.08, rvol_max=1.20, hold=1)),
        ("7 rvol 1.15", dict(q3=-0.03, q10=-0.05, q15=-0.08, rvol_max=1.15, hold=1)),
        ("8 rvol 1.25", dict(q3=-0.03, q10=-0.05, q15=-0.08, rvol_max=1.25, hold=1)),
    ]
    for name, pp in grid:
        p = dict(PARAMS); p.update(pp)
        m = event_mask(f, p)
        wg = _weights_from_mask(ts, o, c, f, m, p)
        _, sg = _metrics(wg, 1.0)
        out["grid"].append({
            "name": name, "params": {k: v for k, v in p.items() if k in
                                     ("q3", "q10", "q15", "rvol_max", "hold")},
            "n_events": int(m.sum()), "exposure": float(np.mean(wg[:, 1])),
            "cagr": sg["cagr"], "max_drawdown": sg["max_drawdown"],
            "sharpe": sg["sharpe"],
        })

    # cuts
    for name, st, en in (("2016-2019", "2016-01-04", "2019-12-31"),
                         ("2020-2021", "2020-01-02", "2021-12-31"),
                         ("2022-2023", "2022-01-03", "2023-12-29")):
        s = _cut(w, st, en)
        out["cuts"][name] = {k: s[k] for k in
                             ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "volatility")}
    for yr in (2020, 2022):
        m2 = mask.copy()
        for d in range(f["nd"]):
            if int(pd.Timestamp(f["dates"][f["last"][d]]).year) == yr:
                m2[d] = False
        w2 = _weights_from_mask(ts, o, c, f, m2, PARAMS)
        _, s2 = _metrics(w2, 1.0)
        out["cuts"][f"ex{yr}"] = {k: s2[k] for k in
                                  ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "volatility")}

    # placebo backtest (200 random event sets)
    out["placebo"] = _placebo(f, int(mask.sum()), n_draws=200)

    dev = out["windows"]["dev"]["1bp"]
    out["status"] = ("1bp_pass_marginal"
                     if dev["cagr"] > 0.3672 and dev["max_drawdown"] < 0.8229
                     else "risk_adjusted_only")

    (OUT / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2, default=float))
    print(json.dumps({k: out[k] for k in ("status", "corr_tqqq", "corr_165d",
                                          "windows", "event_study")}, indent=2))
    print("wrote", OUT / "result.json")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
